raw.assessment: The incumbent offers a repeatable conversational routine, printed access and optional messaging. Seven frequent attendees value its structure, and nine participants regularly rely on print. Its usefulness is uneven: five occasional attendees struggle to enter conversations familiar to their partners, a concrete limit on treating repetition as universally helpful. This does not establish why entry is difficult. Of 72 slips, 49 report ten useful minutes and 48 identify the intended preparation task; 97 attendances occurred, so incomplete reporting and untimed speaking prevent a complete outcome estimate. Coordination sometimes exceeds 90 minutes. Pairing delays and partner changes identify possible friction without proving proficiency mismatch.

openings.claim: Unequal familiarity with the conversation may impede occasional attendees even when the repeated session structure helps frequent attendees. A self-contained opening prompt followed by alternating speaker turns may improve entry while retaining that structure.
openings.delta: Separates familiarity with the routine from familiarity with conversation content; neither public proficiency labels nor attendance prerequisites are needed.
openings.prediction: Pairs using the self-contained opening show fewer early restarts or partner changes and more balanced speaking time; usefulness reports improve particularly among participants reporting unfamiliarity with the topic.
openings.probe: Within existing sessions, offer randomly allocated pairs either usual prompts or the self-contained opening, with voluntary switching. Anonymous observation records entry delay and speaking distribution; exit slips ask usefulness and topic familiarity. Keep the 75-minute limit and log volunteer time.
assumptions: Topic familiarity can be reported anonymously without a proficiency label.
Existing volunteers can prepare the small prompt variation within available time.

openings.claim: Confusion between earlier and next preparation tasks may partly reflect unclear temporal identification on otherwise accessible printed material. A dated, consistently positioned next-session box could reduce that confusion.
openings.delta: Tests task-version recognition separately from speaking-practice quality and does not require digital access.
openings.prediction: Compared with usual sheets, dated boxes reduce earlier-task answers; unchanged blank answers would limit the account to temporal confusion.
openings.probe: Alternate usual and dated sheet formats across six sessions, retaining printed availability at arrival and departure. Count correct, earlier and blank preparation answers separately and record total weekly coordination minutes. Attendance differences limit causal attribution.
assumptions: The next task is settled before printing.
Dates and task wording are understandable to participants.

raw.assessment: The supplied observations establish preparation confusion, variable coordination time and some pairing delays, but do not establish their causes. Exit slips cover 72 of 97 attendances; useful speaking time was not directly measured. Both openings are hypotheses requiring six-session outcome checks.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: immediate neutral pair assignment, self-contained conversation starters and equal timed speaking turns will reduce entry friction while preserving useful practice at different levels. Offer optional simpler or extended prompts without requesting proficiency labels, and allow partner changes.
openings.delta: Retain the familiar session sequence but replace open-ended partner formation and assumed shared topic history with a brief, repeatable entry routine. Use equal turns in a triad when attendance is odd.
openings.prediction: If entry friction and unequal airtime contribute, pairing becomes faster and fewer participants fall below ten useful speaking minutes, including those unfamiliar with the topic. Faster pairing without better usefulness would weaken the proposed mechanism.
openings.probe: Across six sessions, anonymously observe pairing duration and speaking-time distribution; collect participant usefulness reports and optional topic-familiarity responses. Record volunteer preparation and observation time within the weekly coordination total.
assumptions: Timers and prompt choices can be implemented inside 75 minutes with existing volunteers.
Equal airtime alone may not improve usefulness; participant reports remain necessary.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a reusable printed card naming the next session date and one self-contained preparation task will reduce old-task confusion and repeated clarification work.
openings.delta: Print the dated next-task card alongside each current sheet, read it aloud at closing and give it to every attendee. Each task stands alone; returning participants receive current information on arrival and can join without prior preparation.
openings.prediction: Correct next-task identification rises and earlier-task answers fall. If clarification messages decline but total coordination remains above 90 minutes, this mechanism is insufficient for the workload target.
openings.probe: For six sessions, count next-task identification across all attendees and log minutes spent printing, selecting topics, answering messages and arranging access. Track printed-only participants anonymously to check that information access improves for them.
assumptions: Next-session details can be fixed before cards are printed.
Card preparation savings exceed its added printing effort.

openings.claim: Self-contained starters may reduce topic-history barriers while retaining the familiar sequence. A1 additionally proposes neutral immediate pairing, equal timed turns, optional simpler/extended prompts and odd-attendance triads; partner changes remain voluntary.
openings.discriminator: Separate pairing delay, content familiarity and airtime: faster pairing or equal turns without improved reported usefulness is insufficient.
openings.probe: Z1 randomizes pairs between usual prompts and self-contained openings, allowing switching. A1 observes six sessions. Record entry delay, partner changes, speaking distribution, usefulness, optional anonymous familiarity and volunteer time.
openings.uncertainty: Entry causes remain unknown; proficiency mismatch is unproven. Added preparation/timing must fit existing resources.

openings.claim: Z2 proposes a consistently placed dated next-task box to resolve temporal confusion. A2 adds a reusable card with one standalone task, closing read-aloud, universal handout and current information on arrival, potentially reducing clarification work.
openings.discriminator: Separate correct, earlier and blank answers; fewer earlier answers without fewer blanks limits temporal explanation. Fewer messages without total workload below 90 minutes is insufficient.
openings.probe: Z2 alternates usual/dated sheets over six sessions with arrival/departure print access. A2 checks all attendees' identification, anonymous print-only access and printing/topic/message/access time.
openings.uncertainty: Details must be settled before printing and understandable; attendance confounds comparisons, and added printing may offset savings.

Merged with Z2; delivery and workload mechanisms retained.

post_distill.decision: Probe both; no effectiveness established. Preserve free inclusive participation, offline access, conversational purpose, 75 minutes and existing volunteers. Evaluate six-session 80% useful-speaking, 85% preparation and <90-minute coordination targets. Baseline slips cover 72/97 attendances; speaking was untimed and responses unlinked.
